tasks.title: Align product docs around challenge-first success criteria
definition_of_done: `prd.md`, `README.md`, and `docs/status.md` all identify the 12-task local obstacle suite as the primary success bar.
Docs explicitly frame the 10-task bench as regression coverage rather than the product-level outcome metric.
Observable-only evaluation rules are stated in the product contract, not only in `AGENTS.md`.

recommended.approach: Treat doc alignment as a product-contract change first, then update supporting docs to match.

tasks.title: Publish a reproducible challenge proof workflow
definition_of_done: The repo includes a documented and scripted path for `mbus challenge` followed by `mbus package`.
The workflow validates required environment variables and prints exact output artifact paths.
Generated reports and `.ralph` artifacts remain untracked.

recommended.approach: Keep the workflow thin and deterministic: validate env, run the challenge, then package the result.

tasks.title: Document live-eval policy and reframe exploratory config
definition_of_done: A policy doc states that live-site evaluation must use observable interaction only and that hidden deterministic shortcuts do not count.
`challenge.toml` is clearly framed as an exploratory live-eval example rather than the canonical release path.
Top-level docs link the policy so readers do not confuse exploratory work with the primary gate.

recommended.approach: Keep the live-site path documented but explicitly secondary to the reproducible local suite.

tasks.title: Preserve historical notes while marking superseded guidance
definition_of_done: Outdated status and live-site notes include short supersession headers pointing to current docs.
`notes/index.md` labels superseded entries as historical and points readers to the new status docs.
The note corpus preserves chronology instead of rewriting earlier conclusions.

recommended.approach: Annotate only the notes that would materially mislead someone about current direction.

tasks.title: Add a supplemental adversarial obstacle slice
definition_of_done: Supplemental challenge pages cover prompt-injection-style copy and misleading CTA copy without requiring new manifest semantics.
Supplemental manifests use the existing observable-only challenge expectation model.
The primary 12-task default suite remains stable and separate from the adversarial slice.

recommended.approach: Keep adversarial fixtures in a separate tasks directory so the canonical challenge gate does not move accidentally.

tasks.title: Add automated coverage for the supplemental adversarial slice
definition_of_done: Automated challenge coverage exercises the supplemental tasks directory.
The mock-model path can solve the new fixtures and still demonstrates observable-only evaluation.
Quality gates continue to pass after the supplemental suite is added.

recommended.approach: Reuse the existing challenge integration harness so the adversarial slice stays close to the real CLI path.

tasks.title: Generate a real-model challenge proof package
definition_of_done: Run the canonical challenge proof workflow with a real model against the default 12-task obstacle suite.
Produce a packaged report with screenshots, token totals, cost totals, and gate result.
Record the outcome in current status docs or notes without committing generated artifacts.

recommended.approach: Use the scripted proof workflow rather than ad hoc commands so the evidence is reproducible.

tasks.title: Review proof results and decide gate hardening
definition_of_done: Analyze the first real-model proof package for dominant failure buckets and step patterns.
Decide whether the primary gate should remain 10/12, tighten, or require the supplemental adversarial slice.
Capture the decision in `docs/status.md` and, if needed, update `prd.md` and `prd.json`.

recommended.approach: Do not tighten the product gate until there is at least one packaged real-model proof run to evaluate.
